sections.h2: Reaching 100 GW by 2047 means an eleven-fold rise from 9 GW today

chart.title: NPCIL, NTPC and private developers must together cover the 100 GW target

chart.source: Government capacity target; industry NPCIL/NTPC/private split, as reported in the post.
rows: TERI puts investment at Rs 25 lakh crore

sections.todo: Track each developer's commissioned capacity against its announced share so the 2047 target can be checked.

sections.h2: SHANTI cleared Parliament in under a week, yet its licensing rules are still in draft

chart.title: The Act became law in December 2025, but licensing waits on rules not yet final
events: Bill introduced in the Lok Sabha
Published in the Gazette of India as Act No. 39 of 2025
Government tells the Rajya Sabha private applications wait for the rules
Draft SHANTI Rules published; comments closed 4 September
No commencement notification found on the DAE Acts page

sections.means: The Act was passed quickly, but the public record shows no commencement notification and no final rules, so private companies cannot yet apply.
sections.todo: Publish the commencement notification and final SHANTI Rules, and state the date from which private licence applications are accepted.

sections.h2: Foreign reactor projects stay stalled on supplier liability, not on the ownership ban

chart.title: Each stalled foreign project plans six reactors, blocked by supplier liability
chart.sub: Planned reactors per stalled foreign-vendor project.
chart.source: Vajiram & Ravi and Rau's IAS coverage, as cited in the post.

sections.means: Both planned foreign projects have sat stalled for over a decade because vendors will not accept open-ended supplier liability, which SHANTI does not fix.
sections.todo: Pass the separate supplier-liability reform so that foreign vendors can bid for Jaitapur and Kovvada.
